Quantiles, median and robust spread (C backend)

Source: R/prim.R
crob.Rd

cqnt() is the type-7 quantile, R's default, so it agrees with stats::quantile(x, probs). cmed() is the 50% point. cmad() is the median absolute deviation scaled by const so that it estimates the standard deviation of a normal sample. ciqr() is the interquartile range and ctkyfnc() the outlier fences drawn k IQRs beyond the quartiles. A single corrupted row can move a mean or a variance arbitrarily far, but moves a median or a MAD hardly at all, which is what is wanted when screening a column of a released table for values to inspect by hand.

Usage

cqnt(x, probs = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1))

cmed(x)

cmad(x, const = 1.4826)

ciqr(x)

ctkyfnc(x, k = 1.5)

Arguments

x

Numeric (or logical) vector.

probs

Probabilities, each in \([0, 1]\).

const

The scale factor of cmad(), one number from 0: the default 1.4826 is the rounded constant stats::mad() uses, so the two agree exactly; 1 gives the unscaled median deviation.

k

The fence width in IQRs, one number from 0 (1.5 is Tukey's convention, 3 the usual far-out cut).

Value

cqnt(): a numeric vector the length of probs, named as stats::quantile() names it. cmed(), cmad(), ciqr(): a number. ctkyfnc(): a named numeric vector, lower and upper.

Details

The type-7 quantile at probability \(p\) interpolates between the order statistics \(x_{(j)}\) and \(x_{(j+1)}\) with \(h = (n - 1)p + 1\), \(j = \lfloor h \rfloor\): \(Q(p) = x_{(j)} + (h - j) (x_{(j+1)} - x_{(j)})\) (Hyndman and Fan, 1996). The MAD is \(c \cdot \mathrm{median}_i |x_i - \mathrm{median}(x)|\); the IQR \(Q(0.75) - Q(0.25)\); the fences \(Q(0.25) - k \cdot \mathrm{IQR}\) and \(Q(0.75) + k \cdot \mathrm{IQR}\) (Tukey, 1977).

Missing values are not removed: an NA or NaN anywhere makes every result NaN (where stats::quantile() stops). An empty x gives NaN. cqnt() refuses an empty probs and any probability outside \([0, 1]\) or missing.

References

Hyndman RJ, Fan Y (1996). Sample quantiles in statistical packages. The American Statistician 50(4), 361–365. doi:10.1080/00031305.1996.10473566

Tukey JW (1977). Exploratory Data Analysis. Addison-Wesley.

See also

cmom(), ctrmmean().

Examples

x <- c(2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9)
cqnt(x, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))
#> 25% 50% 75% 
#> 4.0 4.5 5.5 
cmed(x)
#> [1] 4.5
cmad(x)
#> [1] 0.7413
all.equal(cmad(x), stats::mad(x))
#> [1] TRUE
ciqr(x)
#> [1] 1.5
ctkyfnc(x)
#> lower upper 
#>  1.75  7.75 
wild <- c(x, 1000)
f <- ctkyfnc(wild)
wild[wild < f[["lower"]] | wild > f[["upper"]]]
#> [1] 1000
cmed(c(1, NA, 3))
#> [1] NaN
try(cqnt(x, 1.5))
#> Error : cqnt: `probs` must lie in [0, 1].
